title: 第24章巧筹粮资稳扎行途第25章故狱相逢得悉冤情
content_zh:
;;
大魏天启十九年秋，秋涝滔天。淮泗大河连日漫堤，骤雨经月不歇，千里平畴尽成泽国。青苗倒伏，屋舍倾颓，阡陌崩毁，舟楫难行。待到雨停水退，遍野尽是烂泥与枯骨。乡野之间，炊烟断绝，老弱僵卧荒村，壮者流离四方，数十万灾民沿官道南下北上，颠沛求生，惨状触目惊心。
天灾已烈，人祸更甚。大魏承平数十载，地方吏治渐腐，州府县衙层层懈怠。灾讯初传京都，朝廷即刻下拨赈灾粮款，令淮泗各州开仓放粮、安抚流民。可诏令一出，层层截留、步步盘剥。州官扣其大半，县官分其余润，乡绅劣绅再借着“代赈”之名私吞克扣。更有商贾豪强趁天灾垄断粮市，封仓囤粮、闭铺拒售，将平日斗米数钱的粮价，哄抬至十倍百倍，以此大发国难之财。
官与绅勾连，吏与商串通，织就一张密不透风的贪腐黑网。朝堂恩泽，半点未入百姓囊中；赈灾粮资，尽数流入私门库房。灾民卖儿鬻女、食草咽土，街巷饿殍枕藉，乡野疫气滋生，而城中权贵依旧锦衣玉食、笙歌不绝，世道偏颇至此，民怨沸腾，乱象暗生。若再不肃贪清弊、筹粮济民，淮泗必生民变，千里疆土或将顷刻崩塌。
危难之际，朝廷摒弃常规吏治拖沓之法，特遣五名精干之人持御赐巡境令牌，入淮泗灾区专司筹粮、肃弊、赈灾、安民事宜。五人各怀绝技、各司其职，性情迥异却同心同德，谋略、风骨、智计、勇武、探查相辅相成，自成一套稳扎稳打的行事体系。为首陈近仇，沉毅持重、胸藏丘壑，深谙朝堂法度与乱世民生，善统筹全局、谋定后动，不喜激进冒进，凡事步步为营，是五人团队的核心主帅。其次包不同，刚正执拗、铁面无私，眼里容不得半分污浊，最擅对账核弊、据理纠偏，不惧权贵、不徇人情，是肃贪正本的利刃。花无艳，玲珑通透、长袖善舞，精通商贾之道、人心博弈与斡旋之术，擅长化解僵局、疏通脉络，以柔智破困局、盘活资源。陈近啸，勇武卓绝、性情刚烈，身手凌厉、杀伐有度，专司镇乱护道、震慑宵小，以铁血手段守护安民大局。铁寻柳，沉静隐忍、心思缜密，擅长暗访探查、追根溯源，善于隐匿行迹、搜集罪证，是团队最隐蔽可靠的耳目斥候。
五人临危受命，辞别京都，不带重兵、不摆仪仗，尽数褪去官服、改换布衣，扮作四方行客微服入境。陈近仇深知，淮泗积弊日久、官绅抱团，利益纠葛盘根错节，若是大张旗鼓、张扬行事，必然打草惊蛇，让一众贪腐之徒提前销毁罪证、转移粮资，最终徒劳无功。故而他定下十字方略：暗访求实、稳扎稳进、先清弊源、再济民生。五人分工明确、层层推进，不贪一日之功、不求一时声名，只求步步落地、件件做实，以朝廷之名肃污浊、以公道之心赈苍生，真正践行替天行道、匡扶社稷的初心。
乱世救灾，首在知情；筹粮安民，根在求实。若不知粮藏何处、弊起何方、冤在何处，一切举措皆是空谈。五人入境淮泗，并未急于对接官府、宣讲政令，而是四散开来，扎根乡野、深入民间，从最底层摸清灾情实况。其中，铁寻柳率先入局，扛起暗访摸排、深挖病根的重任。
铁寻柳常年行走江湖，惯于隐匿行迹、察微知著。他改换粗布麻衣，肩挑货担，扮作走街串巷的杂货小贩，游走于淮泗各州县城、乡野村落、渡口街巷。他不善言辞、不喜张扬，终日沉默行走，看似寻常商贩，实则眼观六路、耳听八方，将四方讯息尽数收纳心中。他深知地方官吏必定虚报灾情、粉饰太平，官文账册皆为虚造，唯有百姓口中的疾苦、街巷流传的传闻、实地所见的景象，才是世间真相。
白日里，他穿梭于流民聚集地、乡镇市集，假意售卖粗盐针线，暗中倾听百姓哭诉疾苦，记录各村各户受灾轻重、断粮时日，摸排豪强囤粮、官吏克扣的蛛丝马迹。夜里，他避开巡街兵丁，潜行于官衙后巷、豪强宅邸外围，探查私仓位置、押运粮船踪迹、官吏深夜密会动向。凡遇深宅大院高墙紧锁、日夜有人看守、寻常人不得靠近的隐秘院落，他必细细标记；凡听闻某乡绅借赈灾之名敛财、某官吏私分粮款的流言，他必多方求证、逐一核实。
彼时淮泗乱象极深，豪强劣绅早已达成默契，统一口径、互相包庇。民间余粮尽数被大户买断封存，市面粮铺空空如也，偶有私售粮食者，皆被豪强打手寻衅打压、强行取缔。官府更是上下一心，伪造粮账、虚报库存，对外谎称灾年无粮、府库空虚，将所有赈灾不力的罪责尽数推给天灾。普通百姓畏惧官绅威势，敢怒不敢言，即便受尽欺压，也无人敢当众揭发。
铁寻柳耐住性子，日夜深耕探查，不骄不躁、不急不迫。他用整整半月时间，走遍淮泗三州十六县，踏遍百余乡野村落，逐一核对各州官衙上报的灾户名册、粮储账目，与民间实情一一比对，梳理出完整的贪腐利益链条。他精准查实：州府官吏七人、县衙官吏二十一人、地方豪强三十九家，相互勾结、层层分利，私吞朝廷专项赈灾粮一十六万余石、赈灾银两万余两，私设隐秘粮仓四十七处，遍布山林别院、废弃驿站、沿河私埠，所有赈灾物资尽数被封存垄断，专供权贵牟利，分毫不予灾民。
不止如此，铁寻柳还探查得诸多隐秘恶行：部分官吏为掩盖亏空，刻意涂改粮账、销毁旧册，将历年存粮尽数划为“灾损核销”；豪强为逼抬粮价，暗中派人损毁民间零星存粮、拦截外来运粮商船，断绝百姓一切求生门路。铁寻柳将所有罪证分门别类、细致归档，何人主谋、何人协办、所得粮资藏于何处、舞弊账目漏洞几何，一一记录在册，字迹工整、条理清晰，桩桩件件皆有实据，无半分臆测虚言。待所有线索摸排完毕、罪证尽数落实，他连夜返回五人隐秘驻地，将厚厚一叠卷宗交付陈近仇，为后续整肃弊政、追缴粮资筑牢最坚实的根基。
底数已明、罪证确凿，接下来便是正本清源、铁面纠弊。此事唯有刚正无私、不避权贵的包不同可担其任。包不同性情耿直、棱角分明，一生恪守公道、笃信法理，最恨为官不仁、为富不义之徒。他不懂圆滑变通，不屑人情世故，面对权贵威压、利益诱惑，始终心如磐石、寸步不让，是五人团队中最锋利、最刚直的一柄利剑。
以往朝廷派员赈灾，多是流于形式、敷衍了事，对地方贪腐多以“从轻处置、下不为例”草草结案，故而地方官吏早已习以为常、有恃无恐。此番见五人入境，州县官员依旧心存侥幸，纷纷备好厚礼、备好说辞，妄图以人情贿赂、虚言搪塞蒙混过关。州官亲自出面，设宴款待、重金馈赠，直言愿私捐薄粮、弥补灾情，只求五人勿深究旧账、不追责过往。一众县官、乡绅紧随其后，纷纷登门示好，或攀附乡情、或许诺重利，极尽拉拢讨好之能事。
面对漫天人情、遍地利诱，包不同悉数拒之门外、分毫不受。他端坐驻地，神色凛然，手持铁寻柳整理的详实罪证，开启逐州逐县、逐人逐案的核查清算。每至一县，他不赴官宴、不收馈赠、不徇私情，当众高悬朝廷赈灾诏令与巡查规制，当众核对官衙存粮账册、灾户登记名册、粮款出入明细。但凡账实不符、数目空缺、登记虚假之处，他当众逐条宣读、当场诘问，不给对方半分狡辩余地。
淮阴县令为官贪婪、行事跋扈，是此次贪腐团伙的核心人物，自持深耕地方多年、人脉广博，面对包不同的核查依旧百般抵赖。他当庭哭诉府库空虚、灾情惨重，谎称自己夙兴夜寐、尽心赈灾，非但无过、反而有功，反诬民间流言皆是流民造谣、有心人恶意中伤。面对这般颠倒黑白的说辞，包不同毫无惧色，当庭出示铁寻柳探查的私仓方位、粮款流转记录、官吏分赃口供，一条条、一桩桩，层层剥开其伪善面具。
包不同立于公堂之上，声如洪钟、字字铿锵：“朝廷发粮赈民，是为生民续命；百姓纳粮完税，是为社稷固本。汝食君禄、居官位，不思安民济世，反而截留赈粮、囤积居奇，眼睁睁看着子民饿死荒野、流离失所，自己坐拥千金、安享奢靡。天灾可恕，人祸难容！此等罪责，无可抵赖、无可宽恕！”
一番怒斥，句句切中要害、字字震彻公堂。淮阴县令面如死灰、无言以对，满堂官吏噤若寒蝉、无人敢辩。包不同顺势依规执法，当场锁拿涉案污吏，封存县衙虚假账册，废除地方私自设立的苛捐杂税与粮市禁令，彻底打破官绅抱团护短的利益壁垒。他行事不偏不倚、不枉不纵，严格区分主犯从犯、首恶胁从，对罪大恶极、屡犯不改的贪官劣绅坚决拿下，对被裹挟、情节轻微的底层吏卒训诫警示、宽大处理，既肃清风气，又避免株连过广、扰动地方安稳。数日之间，淮泗州县贪腐官吏尽数被查、罪责昭然，污浊吏治为之一清，百姓积压已久的怨气得以纾解。
弊源已清、法网已正，最难的一关随之而来——追缴私藏粮资、疏通粮市脉络、筹措赈灾物资。此时官府虚名已破、公信力尽失，豪强虽被震慑，却依旧心存侥幸、抱团抗命，不肯主动开仓放粮。强硬强攻易引发动乱、伤及无辜，温和劝说又难以撼动顽固私利，僵局难解、进退两难。此刻，便轮到心思玲珑、擅长斡旋博弈的花无艳登场破局。
花无艳姿容清雅、气度温润，看似温婉平和，实则智计百出、心思剔透，深谙商贾逐利、世人畏法、豪强惜名的人性根本。她从不执着于单一手段，擅长因地制宜、因人施策，以柔克刚、分层破局，不用刀兵而屈人之私，不用强权而盘活死局。面对错综复杂的粮资困局，她摒弃一刀切的强硬手段，制定出“劝捐、议价、疏渠、保底”四策，层层拆解豪强利益联盟，稳步盘活淮泗粮食市场。

其一为分层劝捐、恩威并施。花无艳将淮泗三十余家囤粮豪强分门别类、精准划分：对家境殷实、囤粮极多、为首牟利的顶级豪强，以律法威慑为主，亮明其囤积居奇、祸乱民生的罪责，明示拒不配合者将抄仓追粮、从严定罪、剥夺功名田产；对跟风囤粮、罪责较轻的中小乡绅，以劝谕激励为辅，晓之以天灾民苦、社稷大义，告知主动捐粮者可登记功德、上报朝廷嘉奖，免除既往轻微罪责，保全家族名声产业。
不少中小乡绅本就是被动跟风，见大势已去、罪责可免，纷纷主动开仓捐粮、上缴余粮。而几名顶级豪强依旧顽固不化、负隅顽抗，妄图凭借家族势力、人脉关系拖延抗拒。花无艳不与其正面争执，转而精准拿捏其软肋：豪门世家最重名声、忌惮祸事，她便将其囤粮害民、漠视苍生的罪证整理公示于州县城门、市井要道，让其恶行昭告天下、颜面尽失；同时断绝其粮船外运、私下交易的所有渠道，封禁其跨州商贸通路，断其牟利后路。
其二为疏通粮渠、平抑市价。淮泗本地粮食被尽数垄断，想要彻底解困，必须引入外来粮源。花无艳凭借多年商贾人脉，连夜修书联络邻州正直粮商、江南粮行巨贾，晓以大义、许以保障，邀请外地粮船入淮泗售粮。同时她报请陈近仇获批政令，新设临时粮市，严令禁止地方势力刁难、盘查外来粮商，保障粮船通行无阻、交易自由。外来余粮源源不断涌入淮泗，彻底打破本地豪强的粮食垄断格局，居高不下的粮价应声回落，百姓终于有粮可购、有米可炊。
其三为规范赈粮、杜绝再弊。花无艳深知，筹粮难、守粮更难，若分发流程混乱、监管缺位，好不容易筹来的粮资依旧会被克扣挪用。于是她亲自拟定《灾民赈粮规制》，效仿历代救荒良法，将灾民分为极贫、次贫、轻灾三等，逐户登记造册、编号盖章，按人头发放粮票、定时定点领粮，杜绝冒领、代领、克扣、私分乱象。同时设立多处便民粥厂，聘请乡中老成笃实之人管理，严格把控煮粥火候、粮食配比，严禁以生水稀释粥食、以霉变粮食充数，避免久饥灾民暴食伤身、染病身亡。细微举措，周全缜密，从根源上杜绝粮资再遭侵占的可能。
筹粮、疏渠、立规诸事稳步推进之际，暗处的危机从未消散。利益受损的豪强势力狗急跳墙，暗中集结护院打手、地痞流氓、亡命之徒，妄图以武力反扑、破坏大局。他们或深夜潜行、纵火焚烧粮仓粥厂；或聚众拦路、劫掠运粮车队；或混入流民之中、煽动民变闹事；或暗中偷袭巡查人员、报复阻挠赈灾。乱世维稳，最怕暗流涌动、突发动乱，一旦局势失控，月余筹粮清弊之功将尽数付诸东流。
此时，勇武凌厉、杀伐有度的陈近啸挺身而出，镇守全局、铁血兜底。陈近啸一身硬功、身法绝世，性情刚烈却不鲁莽，知晓维稳之道不在于滥杀立威，而在于精准镇恶、震慑宵小、保全良善。他不局限于坐守驻地，而是主动出击、全域布防，亲自带队昼夜巡查州县街巷、粮道渡口、粮仓粥厂、流民安置点，全天候守护赈灾秩序与百姓安危。
首当其冲的是流民聚集区的乱象。人多杂乱、饥寒交迫之下，常有流寇趁机偷盗斗殴、抢夺粮食、欺凌老弱。陈近啸巡查期间，遇聚众抢粮者，当场擒拿首恶、惩戒胁从，严明规矩、公示处罚；遇欺凌老弱、哄抢私物者，当即制止、依规处置，绝不姑息纵容。他执法有度、善恶分明，对走投无路、无心作恶的贫苦百姓宽容体恤，对蓄意作乱、恃强凌弱的顽凶零容忍，既稳住了秩序，又收拢了民心。
豪强势力见明面作乱无果，转而动用阴毒手段。城西望族周家，囤积粮食万余石，拒不捐献，暗中雇佣数十名亡命之徒，深夜潜伏于运粮要道，妄图劫掠赈粮、阻断赈灾。当夜月色昏暗、夜风萧瑟，一众暴徒持刀持棍、埋伏林间，待运粮车队途经之时骤然杀出。押粮士卒猝不及防、阵型大乱，局势岌岌可危。
危急关头，陈近啸策马赶至，单骑破局、独挡群凶。他身手迅捷、招招制敌，不恋战、不滥杀，专攻为首作乱之人，片刻之间便制服数名头目，余下暴徒见首领被擒、大势已去，纷纷弃械逃窜。陈近啸当即传令，全境严查亡命余孽，将周家勾结匪类、阻挠赈灾的罪证公示天下，依规查封其所有私仓、尽数追缴囤粮，从严惩治首恶之人。经此一战，所有心怀不轨、妄图武力反扑的势力尽数被震慑，无人再敢妄生歹念、作乱扰民，淮泗治安彻底安稳，筹粮赈灾诸事再无武力阻碍。
四路各司其职、各展所长，而全盘调度、平衡利弊、稳控大局、谋划长远，皆由陈近仇一人统筹执掌。陈近仇身居核心，始终保持清醒克制、沉稳笃定，不被一时战果冲昏头脑，亦不因一时困局焦躁慌乱。他深知，朝廷遣五人替天行道，绝非只为一时赈灾、解一时之危，更在于肃一方吏治、正一方风气、稳一方社稷、谋一方长治久安。故而他行事从不求快、只求实稳，步步推进、层层落地，兼顾惩恶与安民、治标与治本、当下与长远。
在惩恶肃弊之上，陈近仇严守法度、拿捏分寸，令包不同清查案件务求证据确凿、罪责分明，严禁冤及无辜、株连良善；令陈近啸镇乱维稳只惩首恶、不诛胁从，以震慑为主、以惩戒为辅，避免杀伐过重、人心惶惶。对于主动认罪、捐粮赎罪的官吏乡绅，依规从轻处置，给其改过自新之机；对于顽抗到底、作恶多端之徒，坚决从严惩处、绝不姑息，既彰显朝廷法度之严，亦体现仁政宽厚之本。
在赈灾安民之上，陈近仇力求周全公允、普惠万民。他亲自审核花无艳拟定的赈济章程，细化分发流程、完善监管机制，杜绝任何徇私漏洞。针对老弱孤寡、残疾病患、无依流民等特殊群体，设立专项抚恤粮资，优先救助、重点帮扶；针对受灾较轻、尚可自力更生的农户，适度赈济、帮扶复产，避免粮资浪费、滋生惰性。同时采纳古法救荒之策，在流民安置点焚烧苍木醋草、净化空气、驱散瘟气，严防大灾之后必有大疫的隐患，全方位守护百姓性命安危。
在固本长远之上，陈近仇目光深远、未雨绸缪。他清楚知晓，赈灾只能解一时饥渴，复产方能安一世民生。秋涝过后，寒冬将至，若百姓无田可耕、无种可播、无粮可储，来年必定再陷灾荒、再起乱象。于是他统筹调配追缴所得的富余粮资，拆分用途、精准分配：七成粮资用于当下赈济灾民、安稳民生；三成粮资用于修缮被毁农田、修整河道堤坝、购置农具耕牛、储备来年粮种。同时组织流民以工代赈，参与河道修缮、农田复耕、道路整治，既让流民得以劳作饱腹，又能修复地方基建、为来年春耕铺路，一举两得、利在长远。
为彻底杜绝日后粮弊再生、贪腐复燃，陈近仇结合淮泗乱象根源，落地多项长效规制。他下令各州四乡设立官督社仓，择乡中老成公正、善书算、有德行之人担任社正、社副，专人管理、台账公示、定期核查，丰年储粮、荒年赈济，以备不时之需；严令地方官吏每月公示粮库收支、灾情民情，接受百姓监督，杜绝私吞瞒报；划定粮市交易规矩，严禁囤积垄断、哄抬物价，规范商贾经营，从制度层面根除粮市乱象、贪腐土壤。
整整一月有余，五人日夜奔忙、风雨不辍，以稳扎稳打的节奏、各司其职的配合，彻底扭转淮泗危局。铁寻柳隐于暗处、深挖病根，让所有污浊无所遁形；包不同立于明处、铁面纠弊，让所有贪腐罪责难逃；花无艳巧施智谋、盘活僵局，让枯竭粮资重活、闭塞通路畅通；陈近啸铁血镇乱、守护四方，让宵小蛰伏、乱象平息；陈近仇统筹全局、谋定长远，让诸事有序、民生安稳。五人同心、五力合一，不慕虚名、不贪功劳，一心只为安民济世、匡扶社稷。
此番行事，共计追缴公私囤粮、赈灾余粮十八万七千余石，安抚救助受灾流民数十万，查封不法私仓四十七处，惩治贪腐官吏、作恶豪强六十余人，彻底斩断官绅勾结的利益黑链，肃清盘踞淮泗多年的吏治积弊与粮市乱象。跨州粮道全线畅通，粮价平稳回落，粥厂有序运转，流民各得安置，病患得到救治，疫气彻底消散。曾经饿殍遍野、民怨沸腾的淮泗大地，渐渐炊烟复起、人声渐旺，流离百姓纷纷归乡，着手修整屋舍、翻耕农田，乱世颓势尽数逆转，山河重归安稳。
市井乡野之间，百姓交口称颂五人功德。世人皆言，乱世之中，最可贵的从不是惊天动地的侠义壮举，而是步步踏实的为民坚守；最难得的从不是杀伐果断的盖世武功，而是心怀苍生的公道本心。古来替天行道者，多以刀剑斩恶、快意恩仇，逞一时侠气、博一世声名。而陈近仇五人，跳出江湖侠义的狭隘格局，身负朝廷使命、心怀万民苍生，不凭武力横行、不恃权势张扬，以智谋筹粮、以公道肃弊、以安稳济民、以制度固本。他们于细微处破局、于稳妥处成事、于长久处谋利，不求一时快意，但求一方安宁；不求一己功名，但求万民安居。
功成之后，五人并未逗留淮泗、接受百姓馈赠、等候朝廷封赏。待地方秩序彻底稳固、赈灾事宜全面落地、春耕筹备尽数就位，五人悄然收拾行装、连夜启程，奔赴下一处有待整肃的山河。风雨洗尽污浊，山河重归清明，他们来时身负危局、步履匆匆，去时一身坦荡、两袖清风。
大魏江山辽阔，四方隐患未绝，天灾人祸时有发生，污浊弊政尚未尽除。但只要陈近仇、包不同、花无艳、陈近啸、铁寻柳五人尚在，便有公道流转世间、有仁政惠及万民。他们以沉稳定大局、以刚正清污浊、以智谋破困局、以勇武护苍生、以缜密固根基，步步为营、稳扎行途，以朝廷之名匡扶正道，以侠者之心替天行道，护大魏山河无恙，守四海万家安宁。

In the autumn of the 19th year of Tianqi's reign in the Wei Dynasty, there were severe floods. The Huaisi River overflows its embankments day after day, and rain showers persist for months, and the entire country is covered by thousands of miles of flat land. The young crops are lying down, the houses are in ruins, the streets are broken down, and the boats are unable to move. When the rain stopped and the water receded, the fields were filled with mud and dead bones. In the countryside, the smoke is cut off, the old and the weak lie in deserted villages, the strong are displaced in all directions, and hundreds of thousands of victims travel south and north along official roads, struggling to survive. The tragedy is shocking.
Natural disasters are already severe, and man-made disasters are even worse. During the decades of peace in the Wei Dynasty, local officials gradually became corrupt, and government offices in prefectures and counties were slack at all levels. When news of the disaster first reached Kyoto, the imperial court immediately allocated funds for disaster relief and ordered Huaisi prefectures to open warehouses to release grain and appease the refugees. But as soon as the edict came out, they were intercepted and exploited step by step. Prefecture officials deducted most of the profits, county officials divided the remaining profits, and the local gentry and evil gentry embezzled and deducted the profits in the name of "relief on behalf of others." There were even powerful merchants who took advantage of the natural disaster to monopolize the grain market, closing warehouses to hoard grain, closing shops and refusing to sell it. They drove up the price of grain, which was usually worth a pound of rice, to ten or a hundred times, in order to make a lot of money out of the national crisis.
Officials colluded with gentry, and officials colluded with businessmen, creating an airtight black web of corruption. None of the favors from the court went into the pockets of the people; all the food and supplies for disaster relief went into private storehouses. The victims of the disaster sold their sons and daughters, ate grass and swallowed dirt, starved to death in the streets, and plagued the countryside. However, the rich and powerful in the city were still well-dressed and well-fed, playing and singing endlessly. The world was so biased, the people were filled with resentment, and chaos was brewing. If corruption is not eradicated and food is raised to help the people, a civil uprising will occur in Huaisi, and the territory of thousands of miles may collapse in an instant.
At the time of crisis, the imperial court abandoned the conventional method of procrastinating official administration and sent five capable people with imperial patrol orders to the Huaisi disaster area to specialize in raising food, eliminating corruption, providing disaster relief, and reassuring the people. Each of the five people has unique skills and performs their own duties. They have different personalities but share the same goal. Their strategy, character, wisdom, bravery, and exploration complement each other, forming a stable and steady system of their own. The leader is Chen Jinchou. He is prudent and has a deep mind. He is well versed in the laws of the court and the people's livelihood in troubled times. He is good at coordinating the overall situation and making decisions before taking action. He does not like to be radical and hastily advance. He is the core coach of the five-person team. Secondly, Bao BuTong is upright, stubborn, selfless, and can't tolerate any dirt in his eyes. He is best at checking accounts and correcting errors based on reason. He is not afraid of powerful people and shows no favoritism. He is a sharp blade in the fight against corruption. Flowers are not beautiful, exquisite and transparent, long-sleeved and good at dancing. They are proficient in the ways of businessmen, the game of people's hearts and the art of mediation. They are good at resolving deadlocks, clearing connections, breaking through difficulties with gentle wisdom, and optimizing resources. Chen Jinxiao is a man of outstanding martial prowess, strong temperament, sharp skills, and measured killings. He specializes in suppressing chaos, protecting roads, intimidating Xiaoxiao, and guarding the overall situation of peace and security with iron-blooded means. Tie Xunliu is quiet, tolerant and thoughtful. He is good at conducting secret investigations and tracing the source. He is good at concealing his whereabouts and collecting evidence. He is the most covert and reliable spy of the team.
The five people were ordered to bid farewell to Kyoto in the face of danger. They took off their official uniforms, changed into civilian clothes, and entered the country incognito, disguised as travelers from all over the world. Chen Jinchou knew very well that Huaisi had long-standing malpractices, officials and gentry were cliqued together, and entangled interests were intertwined. If he acted with great fanfare and publicity, he would surely alert the snake and allow a group of corrupt people to destroy evidence of crime and transfer food and supplies in advance, which would ultimately be in vain. Therefore, he set a cross strategy: conduct secret visits to seek truth, make steady progress, first eliminate the source of the abuse, and then improve people's livelihood. The five people have a clear division of labor and advance step by step. They are not greedy for one-day achievements or temporary fame, but only seek to implement step by step and do everything concretely. They use the name of the court to eradicate pollution and help the people with justice, and truly practice their original intention of doing justice for heaven and helping the country.
To provide disaster relief in troubled times, the first priority is to be informed; to raise food and bring peace to the people, the root is seeking truth. If we don’t know where the food is stored, where the harm is caused, and where the injustice lies, all measures will be empty talk. When the five people entered Huaisi, they were not in a hurry to contact the government and preach the decree. Instead, they spread out and took root in the countryside and among the people to find out the actual disaster situation from the lowest level. Among them, Tie Xunliu was the first to enter the game and shouldered the important task of making secret visits and digging into the root causes of the disease.
Tie Xunliu travels around the rivers and lakes all year round, and is accustomed to hiding his whereabouts and observing the subtleties. He changed to roughWearing linen clothes and carrying a load of goods on his shoulders, he pretends to be a grocery hawker walking in the streets and alleys, wandering around counties, rural villages, and ferry streets in Huaisi Prefecture. He is not good at words, does not like to show off, and walks silently all day long. He looks like an ordinary merchant, but in fact he sees in all directions and listens in all directions, absorbing all the information from all directions in his heart. He knew very well that local officials would falsely report disasters and whitewash peace, and official account books were all fabricated. Only the sufferings in the mouths of the people, the rumors circulating in the streets, and the scenes seen on the ground were the truth in the world.
During the day, he traveled to refugee gathering areas and township markets, pretending to sell coarse salt needles and thread, secretly listening to the people's cries and complaints of suffering, recording the severity of the disasters in each village and the length of time without food, and looking for clues of the powerful hoarding of food and the embezzlement of food by officials. At night, he avoided the soldiers patrolling the streets and sneaked into the back alleys of government offices and the outskirts of powerful mansions to explore the location of private warehouses, traces of escorted grain ships, and secret meetings between officials late at night. Whenever he came across a secret courtyard that was locked up with high walls, guarded day and night, and not accessible to ordinary people, he would carefully mark it. Whenever he heard rumors that a squire was amassing money in the name of disaster relief, or that an official was secretly sharing grain money, he would seek verification from many sources and verify each one.
At that time, Huaisi was in deep chaos, and the powerful and evil gentry had already reached a tacit understanding, unified their voices, and protected each other. All the surplus grain among the people was bought up and sealed up by large households. Grain shops in the market were empty. Those who occasionally sold grain privately were provoked, suppressed and forcibly banned by powerful thugs. The government worked together to falsify food accounts, falsely report inventories, and lie to the outside world that there was no food and treasury was empty in the disaster year, and all the blame for the ineffective disaster relief was put on natural disasters. Ordinary people are afraid of the power of officials and gentry, and they dare not speak out when they are angry. Even if they are oppressed, no one dares to expose them in public.
Tie Xunliu patiently plowed and explored day and night without being arrogant, impatient, or impatient. He spent half a month traveling across the three prefectures and sixteen counties of Huaisi, and visited more than a hundred rural villages. He checked the lists of disaster victims and grain storage accounts reported by the various prefectures one by one, compared them one by one with the actual situation among the people, and sorted out a complete chain of corrupt interests. He accurately verified that seven state officials, 21 county government officials, and 39 local powerful families colluded with each other to share profits at all levels, and embezzled more than 160,000 dan of special disaster relief grain and disaster relief money from the court. With more than 20,000 taels, forty-seven secret granaries were set up all over the mountains and forests, abandoned inns, and private ports along the river. All disaster relief materials were sealed and monopolized, exclusively for the rich and powerful to make profits, and nothing was given to the victims.
Not only that, Tie Xunliu also discovered many secret evil deeds: in order to cover up deficits, some officials deliberately altered grain accounts, destroyed old books, and classified all grain stocks over the years as "disaster write-offs." In order to force up grain prices, powerful people secretly sent people to destroy scattered private grain stocks, intercepted foreign grain merchant ships, and cut off all means of survival for the people. Tie Xunliu classified and filed all the criminal evidence in detail, including who was the mastermind, who co-organized it, where the obtained food and materials were hidden, and how many loopholes in the fraudulent accounts were recorded in the book one by one. The handwriting was neat and organized. Every piece of evidence was supported by solid evidence, and there was no conjecture or falsehood. After all the clues were sorted out and all the evidence of the crime was confirmed, he returned to the five-person secret station overnight and handed a thick stack of files to Chen Jinchou, laying the solid foundation for the subsequent crackdown on bad governance and the recovery of food and supplies.
The bottom line is clear and the evidence of the crime is conclusive. The next step is to clear up the source and correct the shortcomings. Only Bao Tongtong, who is upright and selfless and does not avoid the powerful, can take responsibility for this matter. Bao BuTong has an upright and sharp temperament. He abides by justice and believes in legal principles throughout his life. He hates officials who are unkind and rich who are unjust. He doesn't know how to be diplomatic and flexible, and he disdains the sophistication of the world. Faced with the pressure of powerful people and the temptation of interests, he always has a rock-like heart and refuses to give in. He is the sharpest and most upright sword in the five-person team.
In the past, the imperial court sent personnel to provide disaster relief, which was mostly a formality and perfunctory. Local corruption cases were often closed hastily with "lenient treatment and no exceptions". Therefore, local officials have long been accustomed to it and feel confident. Seeing five people entering the country this time, state and county officials were still lucky and prepared.He likes generous gifts and prepares good excuses, but tries to get through with bribes and prevarications. The state official came forward in person, hosted banquets, gave large sums of money, and expressed his willingness to donate small amounts of food privately to make up for the disaster. He only asked the five people not to delve into old accounts or hold them accountable for the past. A group of county officials and country squires followed closely behind, and they all came to show their goodwill, either clinging to nostalgia, or promising huge profits, and tried their best to win over and please.
Faced with overwhelming favors and temptations, Bao BuTong refused them all and refused at all. He sat upright at his station with a stern look on his face, holding the detailed evidence compiled by Tie Xunliu, and began to investigate and liquidate state by state, county by county, person by case. Every time he visited a county, he would not attend official banquets, accept gifts, or show personal favoritism. He would hang the court's disaster relief edicts and inspection regulations in public, and publicly check the government's grain account books, the registration list of disaster households, and the details of grain expenditures. Whenever there were discrepancies in the accounts, missing numbers, or false registrations, he would read them out one by one in public and cross-examine them on the spot, without giving the other party any room for quibbles.
The Huaiyin County Magistrate was greedy and domineering as an official. He was the core figure in this corruption gang. He had been deeply involved in the local area for many years and had extensive connections. He still refused in every possible way despite Bao BuTong's verification. He cried in court and complained that the treasury was empty and the disaster was severe. He falsely claimed that he worked hard and worked hard to provide disaster relief. Not only did he have no fault, but he had made meritorious deeds. The false accusations among the people were all made by homeless people and malicious slander. Faced with such confusing rhetoric, Bao BuTong showed no fear. He presented in court the location of the private warehouses that Tie Xunliu had explored, records of grain transfers, and confessions about the division of spoils between officials. One by one, he peeled off his mask of hypocrisy.
Bao BuTong stood in the court hall, his voice was like a bell, and his words were sonorous: "The imperial court distributes grain and provides relief to the people in order to preserve the lives of the people; the people pay grain and pay taxes in order to consolidate the foundation of the country. You are deprived of the emperor's salary and occupy an official position, and do not think about peace and prosperity for the people, but instead But withholding relief food, hoarding it, and watching the people starve to death in the wilderness and live in luxury, natural disasters are forgivable, and man-made disasters are unforgivable!"
An angry rebuke, every sentence hit the mark and every word shook the court. The Huaiyin County Magistrate's face was ashen and speechless, and all the officials in the hall were as silent as cicadas, and no one dared to argue. Bao BuTong took advantage of the situation and enforced the law in accordance with the law. He arrested the officials involved in the case on the spot, sealed the false account books of the county government, abolished the exorbitant taxes and grain market bans set up privately by the local government, and completely broke the interest barrier between the government and the gentry to protect their shortcomings. He acted impartially and without mercy, strictly distinguishing between principal offenders and accomplices, principal offenders and subordinates, and resolutely captured corrupt officials and evil gentry who had committed heinous crimes and committed repeated crimes. He also admonished, warned, and treated leniently low-level officials who were coerced into minor crimes, which not only cleared up the atmosphere, but also prevented excessive implication and disturbed local stability. Within a few days, all corrupt officials in Huaisizhou County were investigated and their culpability was made clear. The dirty officials were eliminated and the people's long-standing grievances were relieved.
Now that the source of the malpractice has been cleared and the legal system has been corrected, the most difficult hurdle is now coming - recovering privately stored grain supplies, clearing up grain market connections, and raising disaster relief materials. At this time, the official reputation has been shattered and all credibility has been lost. Although the powerful officials were frightened, they still took chances and refused to take the initiative to open warehouses and release grain. Tough attacks can easily cause turmoil and hurt innocent people, but gentle persuasion cannot shake stubborn selfish interests. The deadlock is difficult to resolve and the dilemma is between a retreat and a retreat. At this moment, it is the turn of Hua Wuyan, who is thoughtful and good at mediating games, to come on the stage to break the situation.
Hua Wuyan has an elegant appearance and a gentle demeanor. She looks gentle and peaceful, but in fact she is full of wisdom and thoughtfulness. She is well versed in the fundamentals of human nature: businessmen pursue profit, the world is afraid of the law, and powerful people cherish fame. She never sticks to a single method, and is good at adapting measures to local conditions and people, using softness to overcome toughness, breaking situations in layers, subjugating others' selfish interests without using weapons, and reviving dead situations without using force. Faced with the complicated grain dilemma, she abandoned the one-size-fits-all hard-line approach and formulated four strategies of "encouraging donations, negotiating prices, clearing channels, and guaranteeing the bottom line" to dismantle powerful interest alliances at every level and steadily revitalize the Huaisi grain market.
One is to encourage donations at different levels and give both kindness and power. Hua Wu Yan will Huai Si thirtyThe Yu family's grain-hoarding tycoons are divided into categories and precise classifications: the top tycoons, who are well-off, hoard large amounts of grain, and are the leaders in making profits, mainly use legal deterrence to clarify their culpability for hoarding and disrupting people's livelihood. It is made clear that those who refuse to cooperate will have their warehouses raided for grain, severely convicted, and expropriated. To seize fame and property; for small and medium-sized squires who follow the trend of hoarding grain and have relatively minor culpability, they use advice and encouragement as a supplement. They are informed that the victims of natural disasters are suffering and the country is righteous. Those who take the initiative to donate grain are informed that they can register their merits and report to the court for awards. They can be exempted from minor crimes in the past and preserve the family's reputation and industry.
Many small and medium-sized squires were passively following the trend. Seeing that the situation was over and their culpability could be avoided, they took the initiative to open warehouses to donate grain and hand over surplus grain. However, several top tycoons are still stubborn and stubborn, trying to delay the resistance by relying on their family power and personal connections. Hua Wuyan did not argue with him head-on, but instead pinpointed his weakness: the wealthy family valued their reputation most and feared disaster, so she compiled and publicized the evidence of their crimes of hoarding grain and indifference to the people at the gates of prefectures and counties, and in the main streets of the city, so that their evil deeds would be exposed to the world and lose their face. At the same time, they cut off all channels for their grain shipments and private transactions, blocked their inter-state trade routes, and cut off their profit-making opportunities.
The second is to clear grain canals and stabilize market prices. The local food in Huaisi is completely monopolized. If we want to completely solve the problem, we must introduce external food sources. Relying on her many years of business connections, Hua Wuyan wrote a letter overnight to contact the upright grain merchants in neighboring states and the wealthy Jiangnan grain merchants. She promised to invite grain ships from other places to Huaisi to sell grain with the promise of justice and guarantee. At the same time, she petitioned Chen Jinchou to obtain a government order to establish a new temporary grain market, strictly prohibiting local forces from making things difficult and interrogating foreign grain merchants, and ensuring unimpeded passage of grain ships and free trade. A steady stream of foreign surplus grains poured into Huaisi, completely breaking the grain monopoly of the local powerful. The high grain prices fell in response, and the people finally had grains to buy and rice to cook with.
The third is to standardize food relief and prevent further abuses. Hua Wuyan knows very well that it is difficult to raise food and even more difficult to keep it. If the distribution process is chaotic and supervision is lacking, the food funds finally raised will still be withheld and misappropriated. So she personally drafted the "Regulations on Food Relief for Disaster Victims", imitating the good famine relief laws of the past dynasties, and divided the disaster victims into three categories: extremely poor, sub-poor, and minor disasters. They registered and stamped the records on a household-by-household basis, issued food stamps based on head count, and received food at fixed times and at fixed points, to eliminate the chaos of claiming by false claims, receiving on behalf of others, withholding, and private distribution. At the same time, a number of convenience porridge factories were set up, and experienced and reliable people in the township were hired to manage them. The heat of cooking porridge and the proportion of grains were strictly controlled. It was strictly forbidden to dilute the porridge with raw water and use moldy grains to make up the quantity, so as to prevent the people suffering from long-term hunger from overeating, injuring themselves and dying from diseases. Tiny measures and careful measures are taken to fundamentally eliminate the possibility of further misappropriation of food supplies.
While food preparation, canal dredging, and regulations were steadily progressing, the crisis in the dark never dissipated. The powerful forces whose interests were harmed jumped over the wall and secretly gathered thugs, ruffians, and desperadoes in an attempt to counterattack with force and undermine the overall situation. They may sneak around late at night and set fire to granaries and porridge factories; they may gather crowds to block roads and rob food convoys; they may blend in with the refugees and instigate civil unrest; or they may secretly attack inspectors to retaliate and obstruct disaster relief. When maintaining stability in troubled times, we are most afraid of undercurrents and sudden unrest. Once the situation gets out of control, all the efforts made in more than a month to raise food and eliminate defects will be in vain.
At this time, Chen Jinxiao, who was brave, fierce and aggressive, stepped forward to guard the overall situation and fight with iron and blood. Chen Jinxiao possesses hard skills and unparalleled physical skills. He has a strong temperament but is not reckless. He knows that the way to maintain stability lies not in indiscriminate killing to establish power, but in accurately suppressing evil, intimidating Xiaoxiao, and preserving good. He is not limited to staying at the station, but takes the initiative and deploys defenses across the entire territory. He personally leads a team to inspect prefecture and county streets, grain road ferries, granary porridge factories, and refugee resettlement sites day and night, guarding the order of disaster relief and the safety of the people around the clock.
The first thing to bear the brunt is the chaos in refugee areas. With so many people, hunger and cold, bandits often took the opportunity to steal, fight, rob food, and bully the elderly and the weak. During Chen Jinxiao's inspection, he encountered people who gathered to steal food. He captured the culprits on the spot and punished them.Abstain from intimidation, enforce strict rules, and publicly announce punishments; if anyone bullies the elderly or weak, or robs private property, stop them immediately and deal with them in accordance with the rules, and never condone or condone them. He enforces the law with restraint and distinguishes between good and evil. He is tolerant and considerate of poor people who are desperate and have no intention of doing evil, and has zero tolerance for those who deliberately cause chaos and bully the weak. He has stabilized order and won the hearts of the people.
When the powerful forces saw that the rebellion was fruitless, they turned to insidious means. The Zhou family, a prominent family in the west of the city, hoarded more than ten thousand stones of food and refused to donate it. They secretly hired dozens of desperadoes to lurk in the main food transportation routes late at night in an attempt to rob food and block disaster relief. At night when the moonlight was dim and the night wind was cold, a group of thugs armed with knives and sticks lurked in the forest, waiting for the grain transport convoy to pass by and suddenly burst out. The soldiers guarding the grain were caught off guard, their formations were in chaos, and the situation was precarious.
At the critical moment, Chen Jinxiao rushed to the scene, riding alone to break the situation and fend off the group of enemies. He was agile and capable of defeating the enemy with all his moves. He was not fond of fighting or killing indiscriminately. He specialized in attacking those who led the rebellion. He subdued several leaders in a matter of seconds. When the remaining thugs saw that the leader had been captured and the situation was over, they all abandoned their weapons and fled. Chen Jinxiao immediately issued an order to strictly investigate the remaining fugitives throughout the country, make public the evidence of the Zhou family's collusion with bandits and obstructing disaster relief, seize all their private warehouses in accordance with regulations, recover all the grain hoards, and severely punish the culprits. After this battle, all forces with evil intentions and attempts to counterattack with force were deterred. No one dared to have evil thoughts or cause chaos and disturb the people. Huaisi's public security was completely stable, and there was no longer any obstruction by force in raising food and providing disaster relief.
Each of the four groups performs its own duties and demonstrates its strengths, but Chen Jinchou is responsible for overall planning, balancing the pros and cons, stabilizing the overall situation, and planning for the long term. Chen Jinqiu is at the core, always maintaining sobriety, restraint, calmness and determination. He will not be dazzled by the temporary results, nor will he be anxious and panicked by the temporary difficulties. He knew very well that the imperial court sent five people to do justice for heaven, not only to relieve disasters and relieve temporary dangers, but also to suppress the administration of officials, correct the atmosphere, stabilize the country, and seek long-term peace and stability. Therefore, he never seeks speed in his actions, but only pursues stability. He advances step by step and implements layer by layer, taking into account both punishing evil and reassuring the people, treating symptoms and root causes, and the present and the long term.
In addition to punishing evil and eradicating corruption, Chen Jinchou strictly abides by laws and measures, and orders Bao Tongtong to investigate cases to ensure conclusive evidence and clear culpability, and strictly prohibits injustice and innocent people, and implicates good people; Chen Jinxiao is ordered to suppress chaos and maintain stability by only punishing the culprits, not the coercion, focusing on deterrence and supplementing by punishment, so as to avoid excessive killing and panic. For officials and gentry who take the initiative to plead guilty and donate grain to atone for their crimes, they should be dealt with leniently in accordance with the regulations and given the opportunity to reform; for those who resist to the end and commit many evil deeds, they should be severely punished and never tolerated. This not only demonstrates the strictness of the court's laws, but also embodies the foundation of benevolent government.
On top of providing disaster relief and reassuring the people, Chen Jinchou strives to be comprehensive, fair and benefit all people. He personally reviewed the relief charter drawn up by Hua Wuyan, refined the distribution process, improved the supervision mechanism, and eliminated any favouritism loopholes. For special groups such as the elderly, the weak, orphans, disabled people, and homeless people, special food supplies will be set up to give priority to relief and key assistance. For farmers who are less affected by the disaster and can still be self-reliant, appropriate relief will be provided and assistance will be given to resume production to avoid wasting food supplies and breeding inertia. At the same time, ancient methods of famine relief were adopted, such as burning cangwood, vinegar and grass in refugee resettlement sites to purify the air and disperse the plague, so as to strictly prevent the hidden dangers of major epidemics after major disasters and protect people's lives in an all-round way.
On top of consolidating his roots in the long term, Chen Jinqiu has a far-sighted vision and plans for the future. He clearly knows that disaster relief can only relieve temporary hunger and thirst, and resumption of production can ensure people's livelihood for a long time. After the autumn floods, cold winter is approaching. If the people have no fields to cultivate, no seeds to sow, and no grain to store, they will surely fall into famine and chaos again in the coming year. So he coordinated the allocation of the surplus grain recovered from the recovery, divided it into uses, and distributed it accurately: 70% of the grain was used to provide immediate relief to the victims and stabilize people's livelihood; 30% of the grain was used to repair destroyed farmland, repair rivers and dams, purchase agricultural tools and cattle, and reserve grain for the coming year. organize flows simultaneouslyThe people worked for relief and participated in river repair, farmland re-cultivation, and road improvement. This not only allowed the refugees to work hard, but also repaired local infrastructure and paved the way for spring farming in the coming year. It killed two birds with one stone and benefited in the long run.
In order to completely prevent the recurrence of grain fraud and corruption in the future, Chen Jinchou took into account the root causes of chaos in Huaisi and implemented a number of long-term regulations. He ordered all states and towns to set up government-supervised social warehouses, and select senior people from the villages who were impartial, good at calculations, and virtuous to serve as social chiefs and deputy social deputies. They would have dedicated personnel to manage the accounts, publicize the accounts, conduct regular inspections, store grain in good years, and provide relief in lean years to prepare for emergencies; he strictly ordered local governments to Officials should announce the income and expenditure of grain depots and disaster situations and public sentiment every month, accept supervision from the people, and prevent embezzlement and concealment of reports. They should also define rules for grain market transactions, strictly prohibit hoarding, monopoly, and price gouging, regulate business operations, and eradicate chaos and corruption in the grain market from the institutional level.
For more than a month, the five people worked day and night, rain or shine, to completely reverse the crisis in Huaisi with a steady pace and cooperation in performing their respective duties. Tie Xunliu hides in the dark and digs deep into the root of the disease, so that all the filth cannot be hidden; Bao Butong stands in the light and corrects the malpractice, so that all corruption crimes cannot escape; Hua Wuyan cleverly uses wisdom to revitalize the deadlock, so that depleted food resources can be reworked and blocked roads are unblocked; Chen Jinxiao fights iron and blood to suppress the chaos and protects the four sides, allowing Xiaoxiao to lie dormant and the chaos to calm down; Chen Jinchou coordinates the overall situation and plans the long-term, so that everything is orderly and people's livelihood is stable. The five people are of one mind and have five forces united into one. They do not seek vain fame or greed for merit, but are dedicated to reassuring the people, helping the world, and supporting the country.
In this operation, a total of more than 187,000 dan of public and private grain hoards and surplus grain for disaster relief were recovered, hundreds of thousands of disaster-stricken refugees were appeased and rescued, 47 illegal private warehouses were sealed, and more than 60 corrupt officials and evil-doers were punished. All cross-state grain roads are open, grain prices have fallen steadily, porridge factories are operating in an orderly manner, refugees have been resettled, patients have been treated, and the epidemic has completely dissipated. The land of Huaisi, where once people were starving and filled with resentment, gradually started to have smoke from cooking stoves and the voices of people became more and more popular. The displaced people returned to their hometowns one after another, began to repair their houses and plow their farmland. The decline of the troubled times was reversed, and the mountains and rivers returned to stability.
In the streets and countryside, people praised the merits of the five people. Everyone says that in troubled times, the most valuable thing is never the earth-shattering chivalrous feats, but the steady and steady defense for the people; the most rare thing is never the decisive and unparalleled martial arts, but the justice of the common people. In ancient times, those who performed justice on behalf of heaven mostly used swords to kill evil, express grudges and grudges, and show off their chivalry for a while to gain fame for the rest of the world. The five Chen Jinchou broke out of the narrow chivalry pattern of Jianghu. They shouldered the mission of the imperial court and had the common people in mind. They did not rely on force to act rampantly or relied on power. They used wisdom to raise food, used justice to eliminate abuses, used stability to benefit the people, and used systems to consolidate the foundation. They disrupt situations in subtle ways, achieve things in safe places, and seek long-term profits. They do not seek temporary pleasure, but seek peace in one place; they do not seek fame for themselves, but seek peace and stability for all people.
After their success, the five people did not stay in Huaisi to accept gifts from the people or wait for rewards from the court. After the local order was completely stabilized, disaster relief matters were fully implemented, and spring plowing preparations were in place, the five people quietly packed their bags and set off overnight to the next mountain and river that needed to be cleaned up. The wind and rain have washed away the filth, and the mountains and rivers have returned to clarity. When they came, they were in a dangerous situation and walked in a hurry, but when they left, they were magnanimous and had a breeze in their sleeves.
The country of the Wei Dynasty was vast, with hidden dangers in all directions. Natural and man-made disasters occurred from time to time, and the filthy and bad government had not yet been eradicated. But as long as Chen Jinchou, Bao Tongtong, Hua Wuyan, Chen Jinxiao, and Tie Xunliu are still around, there will be justice in the world and benevolent government that will benefit all people. They use calmness to stabilize the overall situation, use uprightness to clean up the dirty, use wisdom to overcome difficulties, use bravery to protect the common people, use meticulousness to solidify the foundation, step by step, make a steady journey, use the name of the court to correct the path, use the heart of a chivalrous person to walk the path of heaven, protect the mountains and rivers of the Wei Dynasty, and keep the peace of thousands of families all over the world.
